name: What is the best way to coordinate multiple consultants on a fast-track project?

mainEntity.name: How should architecture, engineering, interior design, and specialty consultants be managed when the project schedule is compressed?
mainEntity.text: How should architecture, engineering, interior design, and specialty consultants be managed when the project schedule is compressed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fast-track projects only work when coordination is highly organized. A single owner should manage the master drawing set, track consultant inputs, and control revision timing. Review cycles need to be short and deliberate so decisions affecting structure, permit submittal, and long-lead items are made first. The biggest risk on a compressed schedule is that consultants work in parallel without a current reference set. That can lead to mismatched dimensions, conflicting details, and lost time when drawings have to be corrected later. A fast-track process should include frequent milestone check-ins, a clear revision log, and immediate communication when a design change affects another discipline. For luxury residential projects, speed should not replace coordination. It should increase the need for it. Ask how the team handles drawing version control, consultant deadlines, and rapid decision approvals. Those systems are what keep a fast project from becoming a chaotic one.
acceptedAnswer.description: Fast-track projects need a single coordination owner, short review cycles, strict version control, and frequent milestone check-ins. The team should prioritize decisions that affect structure, permits, and long-lead items first. Without a clear schedule and one master drawing set, fast-track projects tend to create avoidable errors.
